items.title: Cost of living protests sweep across Europe

items.title: Morocco commits €366 million to build a national defence industry by 2035
items.snippet: The royal cabinet said the plan aims to meet 40% of the armed forces’ and security services’ equipment needs through domestic production by 2035 and to generate more than 65% of industry revenues from exports, supported by a new strategic agency, a holding company, and two new industrial zones.

items.title: 與 ‘조희대 탄핵’ 착수… “내달까지 소추안 통과”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 20일 조희대 대법원장에 대한 탄핵 추진을 당론으로 채택했다. 대법원이 한덕수 전 국무총리에 대해 유죄 판단을 내리면서도 일부 무죄 취지로 서울고등법원으로 사건을 돌려보낸 지 하루 만에 대법원장 탄핵을 공식화한 것이다. 민주당은 이날 오후 의원총회를 열고 조 대법원장에 대한 탄핵 추진을 당론으로 확정했다. 민주당은 전날 심야 긴급 최고위를 열고 탄핵 추진을 공식화한 데 이어 이날 부산고검장 출신 양부남 의원을 단장으로 하는 ‘조희대 대법원장 탄핵소추 추진단’을 출범시키는 등 ‘탄핵 속도전’에 들어갔다. 민주당은 다음 달까지 탄핵안을 통과시킨다는 계획이다. 대법원장 탄핵소추안은 국회 재적의원 3분의 1(100명) 이상 발의와 과반(150명) 찬성으로 의결할 수 있어 161석의 민주당 단독으로 처리가 가능하다. 민주당은 12·3 비...

items.title: 李 “AI 부정행위 막기 어려워… 국가시험 A부터 Z까지 개편”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 20일 전날 치러진 2027학년도 대학수학능력시험(수능)에서도 부정행위 시도가 이어진 데 대해 “반드시 일벌백계해 달라”며 “국가시험 제도를 A부터 Z까지 전면 신속하게 개편해야겠다”고 했다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 수석보좌관회의에서 “기존 통상적인 방법으로는 더 이상 인공지능(AI)과 첨단 장비를 악용한 부정행위를 효과적으로 막기 어려운 상황”이라며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “이미 진행된 시험의 부정행위에 대해서도 철저한 조사와 엄중한 단죄가 있어야겠다”고 강조했다. 청와대는 임광현 대통령비서실장을 단장으로 한 태스크포스(TF)를 꾸리고 AI·첨단 장비를 활용한 부정행위 근절 및 시험 감독 대책 마련에 나섰다. 정부는 한성숙 국무총리 주재로 수능 부정행위 대응 TF 첫 회의를 열고 사후 추적에 돌입했다. 정부는 전날...

items.title: 與, 선정 기준 논란 ‘민주유공자법’ 강행 처리
items.snippet: ‘민주유공자 예우에 관한 법률안’(민주유공자법)이 20일 더불어민주당 주도로 국회 본회의를 통과했다. 2024년 5월 윤석열 당시 대통령의 재의요구권(거부권) 행사로 폐기된 지 2년 반 만에 국회에서 처리된 것이다. 민주당은 이날 본회의에서 국민의힘이 전날부터 이어 온 필리버스터(무제한 토론)를 강제 종결하고, 국민의힘이 표결에 불참한 가운데 재석 의원 178명 찬성으로 법안을 가결했다. 민주유공자법은 1964년 3월 24일 이후 민주화운동 과정의 사망·행방불명·부상자에게 의료·양로·요양 지원을 하는 내용을 담고 있다. 4·19혁명과 5·18민주화운동 관련자들이 별도의 법률에 근거해 유공자로 예우받는 것과 달리 6월 민주항쟁 및 부마 민주항쟁 등의 관련자들이 합당한 예우를 받지 못하고 있다는 지적을 반영한 것. 국가보훈부에 따르면 민주유공자법...

items.title: 범여권 186명중 150명 찬성 탄핵안 통과땐 대법원장 직무정지
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 조희대 대법원장 탄핵소추를 당론으로 확정하면서 41년 만에 대법원장에 대한 탄핵 절차가 본격화됐다. 1985년 불공정한 법관 인사를 했다는 이유로 발의된 유태흥 대법원장 탄핵안은 12대 국회에서 부결됐지만 조 대법원장에 대한 탄핵안은 민주당을 포함한 범여권이 탄핵소추안 의결에 필요한 과반 의석수를 훌쩍 넘어서는 186석을 확보하고 있는 만큼 통과될 가능성이 크다. 헌정사상 첫 대법원장 탄핵 의결과 직무 정지가 현실화될 수 있다는 것. 이에 따라 내년 2월 법관 정기인사에도 영향이 불가피할 것이란 전망이 나온다.● 與 지도부 탄핵 속도전… 당내 일각 “명분 없는 탄핵”민주당은 20일 오후 국회에서 의원총회를 열고 조 대법원장에 대한 탄핵소추를 당론으로 채택했다. 당론 추인은 별도의 표결 절차 없이 지도부가 탄핵 결정을 보고하는 방...

items.title: 국힘 “판결엔 불복, 대법원장엔 보복” 릴레이 장외투쟁 여론전
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 조희대 대법원장에 대한 탄핵소추 추진을 당론으로 채택하자 국민의힘은 “광기이자 보복”이라고 반발했다. 국민의힘은 민주당의 조 대법원장 탄핵 추진을 “조작기소 특검 국면 전환을 위한 꼼수”라고 규정하고 총력 저지에 나서겠다는 입장이다. 정점식 원내대표는 20일 오전 조작기소 특검 규탄 도보행진을 위해 서울 마포구 홍익대 인근에서 열린 현장 원내대책회의에서 “재판 결과가 마음에 안 든다고 해서 대법원장 한 사람을 상대로 반역이니, 내란이니 운운하면서 탄핵을 추진하는 것은 광기일 뿐”이라고 말했다. 이어 “내란은 그저 구실에 불과하다. 저들의 본심은 결국 이재명 대통령의 공직선거법 위반 유죄를 확정 지은 파기환송 판결에 대한 복수심”이라며 “결국 이 대통령 한 사람을 위한 무자비한 정치 보복”이라고 주장했다. 민주당이 한덕수 전 국무...

items.title: “계엄 요건 못갖춰, 군경 동원은 위헌-위법” 대법-尹 1심 동일 판단
items.snippet: 대법원이 한덕수 전 국무총리의 내란 중요임무 종사 사건에서 12·3 비상계엄의 위헌·위법성을 명확히 하고 윤석열 전 대통령의 국헌문란 목적을 뒷받침하는 판단을 내놓으면서 관심은 윤 전 대통령의 내란 우두머리 혐의 재판에 어떤 영향을 미칠지에 쏠리고 있다. 내란 사건에 대한 첫 대법원 판결문에서 윤 전 대통령의 이름은 총 104차례 언급됐다. 윤 전 대통령의 내란 우두머리 혐의 재판 항소심은 내년 1월 선고된다.● 대법원 “계엄 당시 국가비상사태 없었다”대법원 전원합의체는 19일 12·3 비상계엄이 “그 자체로 위헌·위법함에는 의문의 여지가 없다”고 밝혔다. 대법원은 “전시·사변 등에 준하는 국가비상사태가 발생하지 않았다”며 “그런데도 군과 경찰을 동원해 국회와 언론사 등을 장악하려 한 것은 헌법 질서에 어긋난다”고 못 박았다. 이는 윤 전 대...

items.title: 李, YS 추모식서 “개혁이 혁명보다 어려움 느껴”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 20일 김영삼 전 대통령 서거 11주기를 맞아 “후배 국정 책임자가 돼 보니 ‘개혁이 혁명보다 어렵다’고 하셨던 말씀의 무게를 느끼게 된다”고 밝혔다. 이 대통령은 이날 서울 동작구 국립서울현충원에서 열린 추모식에서 최인호 대통령정무수석비서관이 대독한 추도사를 통해 “기득권의 벽을 정면으로 돌파했던 거산(巨山)이라는 튼튼한 반석이 있었기에 저를 비롯한 후배들은 변화를 차곡차곡 쌓아 올릴 수 있었다”며 이같이 말했다. 이 대통령은 또 “대통령님께서는 금융실명제를 단행해 낡은 시대를 끝내셨다”며 “국민주권정부는 대통령님의 뜻을 이어 주가 조작과 시세 조종 세력을 엄단하고 부당 이득을 철저히 환수하며, 시장 질서를 흔드는 행위를 뿌리 뽑겠다”고 했다. 이어 “자본시장과 민생 경제에 있어 ‘비정상의 정상화’를 반드시 이뤄낼 것”이라고...

items.title: 李대통령 국정평가 긍정 40%-부정 49%
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령 국정수행에 대한 긍정 평가가 40%, 부정 평가가 49%로 집계됐다. 한국갤럽이 17∼19일 전국 유권자 1001명을 대상으로 실시해 20일 발표한 여론조사(전화면접 방식·95% 신뢰수준에 표본오차 ±3.1%포인트·자세한 사항은 중앙선거여론조사심의위원회 홈페이지 참조)에 따르면 이 대통령이 “잘하고 있다”는 답변은 40%, “잘못하고 있다”는 답변은 49%였다. 지난주 조사에선 각각 39%, 50%였다. 긍정 평가 이유로는 외교(24%)와 경제·민생(12%) 등이 많았고 부정 평가 이유로는 경제·민생(18%), 도덕성 문제·본인 재판 회피(13%), 부동산 정책(12%) 등을 많이 꼽았다. ‘향후 1년간 우리나라 경제가 좋아질 것’이라는 낙관 전망은 26%, ‘나빠질 것’이란 비관 전망은 38%였다. 경기 낙관론은 올 6월까지...

items.title: 김건희 “도이치 주가조작 유죄, 죽어도 이해 못해”

items.snippet: 과거 검찰이 수사권을 남용했는지 조사하겠다며 출범한 검찰인권존중미래위원회(검찰미래위)는 20일 진상조사단에게 위례 신도시 개발 비리, 문재인 정부 부동산 통계 조작 사건과 관련한 보완조사 결과를 다시 보고받았다. 지난달 15일, 이달 5일에 이어 세 번째 보고다. 진상조사단은 두 차례 추가 보완조사에도 여전히 “검찰 수사에서 위법성을 발견하지 못했다”고 보고했는데도, 검찰미래위는 결론을 내지 않고 있다.

items.title: 중증 감염병인데… 항생제 투여 하루만에 등교를?
items.snippet: 일선 학교에 배포된 감염병 예방·위기 대응 매뉴얼이 오히려 현장에 혼란을 주고 있다. 중증 감염병에 걸린 학생에게 항생제 치료 하루 만에 등교를 해도 되는 것처럼 나와 있거나, 감염 여부를 제대로 알 수 없는 시점을 ‘등교 중지 기간’으로 정하는 등 이를 그대로 적용하기 어렵다는 지적이 나온다. 바로 교육부와 질병관리청 등이 2023년 12월 만든 학교 감염병 대응 매뉴얼이다.

items.title: “지방서 일할 의사 모십니다” 일당 100만원 주고, 은퇴한 70대 채용
items.snippet: 충북 충주시는 이달 초 70대 초반의 퇴직 전문의를 기간제 의사로 채용했다. 지역 내 공중보건의사(공보의)가 줄자, 기간제 의사를 보건지소(읍·면 단위 공공의료기관) 순회 진료에 투입하기로 했다. 과거 13명이던 의과 공보의가 지금은 2명만 남아 있고, 이들마저 내년 4월 복무를 마치면 한 명도 남지 않기 때문이다. 시 관계자는 “기간제 관리 의사 추가 채용도 검토 중”이라고 했다.

items.title: [알립니다] 치매 진단·치료법 알려드려요
items.snippet: 삼성서울병원과 조선일보사가 마련하는 ‘랜선 건강교실’ 11월 영상이 업로드됐습니다. 이번 건강교실 주제는 ‘치매’입니다. 현대 사회에서 가장 두려운 뇌 질환으로 꼽히는 치매에 관한 진단과 치료 방법 등 다양한 궁금증을 삼성서울병원 신경과 김희진 교수가 자세히 풀어드립니다.

items.title: 주말까지 춥다… 체감 영하 10도
items.snippet: 절기상 소설(小雪)인 22일 아침까지 영하권 추위가 이어지겠다. 바람도 강하게 불면서 중부 내륙에선 체감온도가 영하 10도 안팎까지 내려갈 것으로 예상된다. 호남과 제주에는 21일까지 눈이 내리겠다.

items.title: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh pledges ‘relentless diplomacy’ in bid to lead the UN
items.snippet: Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati star diplomat running to succeed António Guterres, told Euronews the UN must return to its core purpose of peace, development, and prosperity. She has pledged relentless diplomacy, a leaner UN judged on results, and early action on wars from Ukraine to Gaza if chosen.

items.title: 화재 현장서 외국인 16명 대피 도운 박진용씨 ‘용감한 의인’ 서울시 표창
items.snippet: 서울시 소방재난본부는 지난 1일 관악구 숙소 화재 현장에서 외국인 투숙객 16명을 대피시킨 회사원 박진용(37)씨에게 ‘재난 현장 용감한 의인’ 표창을 수여했다고 20일 밝혔다. 당시 오토바이를 타고 지나가던 박씨는 숙소에서 불길이 치솟자 곧바로 119에 신고했다. 오후 2시 18분쯤이었다. 이어 불이 난 3층으로 올라가 객실 문을 두드리며 “불이야”라고 외쳤다. 스페인 단체 관광객 12명 등 외국인 투숙객 16명은 그제야 불이 난 사실을 알고 대피했다. 불은 2시간여 만에 꺼졌고 인명 피해는 없었다. 서울시는 “박씨가 위험한 상황에서도 용기 있는 행동을 했다”고 했다. 박씨는 “연기가 많이 나서 안에 있는 사람들에게 알리려고 올라갔다”며 “당연한 일을 했을 뿐”이라고 했다.

items.title: “한류, 잠깐의 유행 아닌 학문으로 남길 겁니다”
items.snippet: 영국 옥스퍼드대의 유서 깊은 회의장 ‘콘보케이션 하우스’에 판소리 가락이 울려 퍼졌다. 900년 넘는 이 대학 역사상 처음으로 ‘한국학센터(The Oxford Centre for Korean Studies)’가 지난 19일 문을 열었다. 초대 소장을 맡은 조지은(50) 교수는 “처음 영국에 온 25년 전엔 상상도 못한 장면이라 가슴이 벅찼다”고 했다. 석·박사까지 배출할 수 있는 한국학센터 출범으로 옥스퍼드대 내 한국학 강의가 대폭 늘고 다양해질 전망이다.

items.title: 박승일 아산의료원장·이제환 서울아산병원장

items.snippet: The COP31 climate conference slipped into overtime on Friday as negotiators from nearly 200 ⁠countries struggled to bridge deep divisions ⁠over fossil fuels and climate finance. Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference ⁠heaped pressure on host Turkey and lead negotiator Australia, saying the meeting was on track to be the “worst COP ever” because it lacked ambition to address the worsening climate crisis...

items.title: 나이 듦이 가져다주는 선물 [고혜련의 삶이 있는 풍경] (29)
items.snippet: 겨울을 향해 손짓하며 찬연한 오색 단풍과 낙엽이 천지를 물들이는 늦가을. 사계절이 있는 이 강토가 새삼 고맙다. 사계절은 마치 인간들에게 주어진 생명의 변화를 잘 살피도록 짜인 각본 같다. 천지를 찬란하게 물들이며 아름다움을 뽐내는 늦가을을 그냥 보내는 게 ‘예의가 아닌 듯해’ 단풍이 절정인 곳을 찾아 나섰다. 단풍의 황홀함에 대한 뻔한 찬사 같지만 아니다. 자연에 빠져 인생 행로조차 바꾼 사람에게 대자연을 칭하는 ‘마더 네이처(Mother Nature)’가 만물의 위대한 어머니, 조물주의 사랑으로 다가오는 것에 응답하기 위해서다. 이파리를 모조리 떨궈 자신의 온몸을 흙으로 내려놓는 나무의 자태가 절묘하고 숭고한 섭리로 보인다. 일견 “이제 준비하라”는 귀띔 같다. 나이가 들긴 들었나 보다. 나이 듦이 가져다주는 선물은 감사한 마음이 보다 자...

items.title: 양재천의 만추
items.snippet: 걷는 걸 즐기게 되면 생활의 많은 게 달라진다. 같은 거리도 차를 타고 다닐 때는 보이지 않던 것들을 볼 수 있게 된다. 그래서 약속 장소가 그리 멀지 않고 시간적 여유가 있는 날에는 되도록 걸어간다. 먼 곳이라 차를 타고 가야 하는 경우에도 30분에서 한 시간 정도 일찍 도착해 주변을 구경하며 산책하듯 걷는다. 이런 여유가 일상에 자리 잡으면 길이 막혀 약속에 늦는 결례도 줄일 수 있다.

items.title: 한반도 밀고 들어온 중공군, 포로 75%는 왜 본국 귀환을 거부했나
items.snippet: 중국인민지원군(중공군)과 국군·유엔군의 최초 교전은 1950년 10월 25일 평안북도 운산에서 벌어졌지만, 중국공산당은 6·25전쟁 발발 1년 전부터 북한에 대규모 병력을 지원했다. 1949년 4월 마오쩌둥은 북로당이 요청한 중국인민해방군 소속 3개 한국인 사단의 북한 파병에 동의했다. 해방 이전 조선의용대는 중국공산당 팔로군과 연합해 항일무장투쟁을 전개했다. 해방 후 이들은 인민해방군 제4야전군에 배속돼 국공내전에서 장제스의 국민혁명군(국민당군)에 대항해 싸웠다. 이렇듯 실전 경험이 풍부한 정예 병사 최소 3만7000명이 1949년 7월부터 1950년 5월까지 북한으로 이동해 조선인민군(인민군)에 편입됐다. 6·25전쟁 개전 당시 남침 선봉에 섰던 인민군 21개 연대 중 10개 연대, 병사의 40% 내외가 이들 중국인민해방군 출신 한국인 병...

items.title: 엄마가 그리운 날엔 ‘엄마 어렸을 적엔’ 이야기 속으로…
items.snippet: 지금으로부터 30년 전, 많은 국민의 공감을 불러일으킨 못난이 인형들이 있었다. 1960~1970년대 순박하고도 정이 넘쳤던 우리 부모 세대의 자화상을 닮은 이 못난이 인형들을 들여다보며 어떤 이는 눈물짓기도, “그땐 그랬지~” 하며 고개를 끄덕이기도 했다. 1996년 조선일보미술관 전시를 비롯해 예술의전당, 지방 전시장을 순회하며 180만 관람객을 불러 모았던 이승은·허헌선 부부의 인형전 ‘엄마 어렸을 적엔…’ 얘기. 당시 전시를 통해 ‘데뷔’한 못난이 인형들은 이후 초·중·고 교과서에도 실릴 만큼 화제가 되며 ‘국민 인형’ 못지않은 인기를 누리기도 했다.

items.title: 이미륵상
items.snippet: 이미륵상은 한독협회와 독한협회가 1999년 이미륵 박사 탄생 100주년을 기념해 제정한 상입니다. 이미륵 박사는 1899년 황해도 해주에서 태어나 서울에서 의학 공부를 하던 중 3·1운동에 참여했다가, 일제의 수배를 피해 상하이를 거쳐 독일로 망명했습니다. 그곳에서 의학 및 생물학을 공부하는 한편 자전적 소설 ‘압록강은 흐른다’를 집필하는 등 한국의 문화와 정신을 독일 사회에 알렸습니다. 이미륵상은 이미륵 박사의 뜻을 기리고 한국과 독일의 문화 교류 및 상호 이해 증진에 기여한 인사에게 한독협회와 독한협회가 해를 바꿔가며 수여하는 상입니다.

items.title: 한국의 의료계가 ‘성역’이라고?
items.snippet: 올 하반기 소아청소년과 전공의 모집 정원이 119명인데, 2명 지원했다. 이대로 가면 소아청소년과 의사의 씨가 마를 판이었다. 그런데 엎친 데 덮친 격이라고 그 와중에 아주대 소아응급실 압수수색 사태까지 터졌다. 이제 다음 번 전공의 모집 때는 지원자가 아예 제로로 떨어지는 것은 아닐까? 그야말로 소아청소년 진료라고 하는 우리 의료의 한 분야 자체가 붕괴될 지경이다. 그런데, 놀랍게도 우리 사회 일각에서는 볼멘소리도 나오는 것 같다. ‘의사가 성역이냐?’는 것이다. ‘의사도 국민인데, 범죄신고가 들어오면 압수수색도 받고 진료하다 환자가 죽으면 형사처벌을 받는 것이 당연하지 않느냐’는 것이다.

items.title: 일타 강사인가 ‘일탈’ 강사인가

items.title: 실용적이고 눈에 띄어… 비녀 사러 갑니다
items.snippet: 16일 낮 1시쯤 서울 종로구 동대문종합시장 액세서리상가. 한 외국인이 나비 장식이 달린 옥색 비녀를 집어 들었다. 그러고는 같은 제품 여섯 개를 결제했다. 미국인 관광객 세라(50)씨는 “한국적인 디자인이 많아 고급스러워 보이는 데다 실용적”이라며 “선물용으로 여러 개 산 것”이라고 했다. 한복을 입을 때 주로 쓰던 전통 장신구인 비녀를 찾는 이들이 늘고 있다. 비녀가 평상복에도 어울리는 머리 장식으로 자리 잡고 있는 것이다. 외국인 관광객 사이에서는 한복 체험 때 잠시 꽂는 소품을 넘어 일상에서 쓸 수 있는 ‘한국식 패션 아이템’으로 인기를 끈다. 머리를 간단히 틀어 올려 고정할 수 있는 데다 하나만 꽂아도 눈에 띄는 장식이 된다는 점이 인기 요인으로 꼽힌다.

items.title: 소음에 귀 기울이지 말라 [안광복의 주말의 철학]
items.snippet: 로마 장군 파비우스 막시무스의 별명은 ‘굼뜬 사람(cunctator)’이었다. 한니발이라는 무시무시한 적장에 맞선 그의 군대는 좀처럼 싸우려 나서지 않았다. 보급선을 위협하며 소소한 싸움만 걸었을 뿐이다. 조급해진 로마 시민들의 비난이 빗발쳤다. 그래도 파비우스는 묵묵히 끈질기게 한니발의 뒤를 따라다니기만 했다. 마침내, 전쟁이 끝났을 때 ‘굼뜬 사람’이라는 별명은 최고의 영예가 됐다. 만약 막강했던 한니발의 군대와 크게 한판 붙었으면 로마의 군단은 결딴났을 터다. 파비우스가 충분히 시간을 끌어주었기에, 로마는 그에게 맞설 만큼 힘을 기를 수 있었다.

items.snippet: 대학수학능력시험(수능)을 하루 앞둔 18일 문구를 파는 매장 곳곳에서 때아닌 연필 품절 사태가 벌어졌습니다. 연필깎이도 함께 동났습니다. 업계는 그 이유로 이날 오전 교육부가 발표한 ‘시험장 휴대 가능 물품 변경’ 안내를 꼽았습니다. 교육부는 필기구 반입 기준을 바꿔 수험생이 가져갈 수 있는 필기구를 ‘흑색 연필’로 제한했습니다.

items.title: 뒤집어 알고 있던 것들
items.snippet: 왼쪽 아래 송곳니가 길고 날카롭다는 느낌에 한동안 불편했다. 입을 다물 때마다 아래 송곳니가 윗니와 먼저 닿는 느낌이었다. 대개 몸의 어떤 부위가 의식되고 신경 쓰인다는 건 그 자리에 문제가 있다는 신호다. 의식하면 더 나빠진다. 캐스터네츠처럼 윗니와 아랫니를 딱딱 치는 습관이 생겼다. 치과에서 엑스레이를 찍어보니 이 습관이 문제였다. 씹는 힘을 지속적으로 받는 송곳니 끄트머리가 마모되고 떨어져 나가 손상되지 않은 부위, 온전한 치아가 길고 날카롭게 느껴졌던 것이었다. 의사가 엑스레이 화면에 치아가 떨어져 나간 자리를 그려 설명해줬다. 솟은 자리가 아니라 떨어져 나간 자리였다니, 뒤집어 알고 있었다.

items.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
items.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. items.title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
items.abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar exciton...

items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

items.title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
items.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. items.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
items.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. items.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. items.title: Asymmetric Transistor Aging Under Thermal Gradients
items.abstract: Advanced technology nodes improve performance but increase susceptibility to BTI-induced aging. Using aging- aware circuit simulations, we show that realistic on-chip thermal gradients can cause significant asymmetric transistor degradation in 16 nm FinFET circuits, leading to setup and hold time violations. These results highlight the necessity of incorporating thermal-gradient-aware aging analysis into timing signoff to ensure chip reliability.

items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Atomic-scale assembly of sulfur vacancy complexes for tailored in-gap states in monolayer WS$_{2}$
items.abstract: Atomic-scale defects in two-dimensional semiconductors are quasi-isolated quantum systems with promise for emerging technologies. Although their potential as spin qubits, quantum sensors and single-photon emitters has been demonstrated experimentally, creating them deterministically and identifying them chemically remains challenging, which limits control over their electronic states. In this work we assemble sulfur vacancies in monolayer WS$_{2}$ into complexes of different sizes and geometries using the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope. We study their electronic properties by a combination of scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory, revealing the intricate influences of geometry, underlying point group symmetries and spin-orbit coupling on hybridized states. items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

items.title: Delay Mismatches Shape the Spectra of Three Synchronized Semiconductor Lasers
items.abstract: We study a network of three synchronized chaotic lasers and the radio frequency spectra of the intensity fluctuations. The position and morphology of the peaks are significantly different depending on the set of lasers being synchronized. The lasers and coupling paths are similar but not identical in all parameters, including their feedback and coupling delay times. The inverse of the delay mismatch between each pair of lasers introduces characteristic frequencies that shape the spectral response of the synchronized system. By studying two different three-laser configurations, we find that peaks appear whenever multiple harmonic contributions overlap in frequency, resulting in constructive enhancement of the spectral power. items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one...

items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. items.title: A Probabilistic Behavioral RTL Simulation Framework for Probabilistic Compute Fabrics
items.abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. items.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
items.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. items.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
items.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.abstract: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. items.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
items.abstract: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. items.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU
items.abstract: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. items.abstract: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. items.abstract: Topological insulator field-effect transistors (TIFETs) have emerged as a promising alternative to overcome the scaling limits of silicon-based field-effect transistors (Si-based FETs). items.abstract: The generation and control of circularly polarized and chiral light is important for a wide range of applications, from sensing to optical communication and catalysis. We exploit the $π$/2 phase difference between the transverse and longitudinal components of the electric field that is carried by 30 keV electrons, to coherently excite degenerate dipolar modes of which the far-field radiation interferes in the far field, thereby creating a strong optical spin-Hall effect. items.title: Koopmans spectral functionals for excitons in materials
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles characterization of excitons typically relies on the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) combined with quasiparticle energies from computationally demanding GW calculations. Here, we replace the GW step with quasiparticle energies from Koopmans-compliant spectral functionals, an approach we call BSE@qKI, and implement it in an automated, reproducible AiiDA workflow. For a set of benchmark semiconductors, BSE@qKI reproduces experimental band gaps and first exciton energies with mean absolute relative errors of 13% and 4%, respectively, comparable to BSE@G0W0 for the gaps and markedly better for the excitation energies. We also apply the method to the layered magnetic semiconductor CrI3, obtaining an absorption spectrum that reproduces the main experimental features. These results establish BSE@qKI as a GW-free alternative to BSE@G0W0 for systematic studies of excitonic...

items.title: A Discrete Digital Isolator with Shielded Planar Transformer for Gate Driver Applications
items.abstract: Galvanically isolated gate drivers are required in many power electronics applications. This paper describes an implementation of a digital isolator using discrete components with a planar coreless PCB signal transformer providing the isolation. The use of an electrostatic shield between the transformer windings is shown to provide sufficient common-mode transient immunity to support IGBT half-bridge drivers, an application subject to a severe dV/dt transient during switching. The design is verified through the experimental implementation of a prototype half bridge using two of the proposed discrete digital isolators with SiC power transistors and demonstrates common-mode transient immunity greater than 15 kV/us with very low implementation complexity.

items.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
items.abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width from 1 to 6, reproduces the standard integer and floating-point formats exactly, and comes within 0.07 bits of the ideal at 4 bits. It matches a random...

items.title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
items.abstract: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody. We analyze a 3D box with such mirrors as walls to accumulate and store blackbody radiation. Applications include solar-powered thermal energy and solar-powered thermophotovoltaics. items.title: Optical characterization of Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride
items.abstract: Amorphous silicon nitride is the leading low-loss, CMOS-compatible platform for wafer-scale integrated photonics. Encapsulating transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers within this platform offers a promising route towards scalable TMD-photonic circuits. Yet the effect of this amorphous dielectric on the optical response of the monolayer remains poorly understood. Here, we compare monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride with a hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated reference, using differential reflectivity and photoluminescence. Whereas the reference is dominated by the neutral exciton, the nitride-encapsulated monolayer shows attractive and repulsive polaron resonances separated by ${\sim}31$~meV, with emission dominated by the attractive branch. items.abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are attractive for space applications because they combine high detection efficiency, low noise, and fast timing, but their radiation tolerance remains less established than that of conventional semiconductor detectors. Here we study NbN SNSPDs exposed to alpha-particle $^{210}$Po irradiation by combining cryogenic electrical and photon-counting measurements with SRIM and Geant4 radiation-transport calculations. For the estimated fluence corresponding to the 200-hour $^{210}$Po exposure, the air-inclusive Geant4 calculation predicts an average ionizing dose of 8.49 Mrad in the active NbN layer and a displacement-damage estimate of $5.67 \times 10^{-7}$ displacements per atom. items.abstract: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. The surrogate maps compact-model parameters and device geometry to the complete set of output and transfer characteristics. Extraction is a bounded least-squares search: a bank of NGSpice simulations supplies initial candidates, finite differences of the surrogate supply the local Jacobian, and NGSpice re-simulates the resulting cards before selection. items.title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
items.abstract: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. items.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
items.abstract: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. items.title: A Hierarchically Compressed Immittance Operator Formulation for Fast Statics-to-Full-Wave Electromagnetic Simulation with the Boundary Element Method
items.abstract: The boundary element method allows the electromagnetic simulation of three-dimensional problems with a two-dimensional discretization, using a surface integral representation of Maxwell's equations. For applications involving broadband simulations or multiscale geometries, the well-known low-frequency breakdown of conventional integral equation formulations must be addressed, while ensuring that dielectric, semiconducting, and lossy metallic regions are modeled rigorously, including the skin effect. In this work, a new boundary element formulation based on an immittance operator is proposed, where the underlying integral equations are inherently valid from statics to the full-wave regime. items.title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
items.abstract: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. items.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
items.abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed...

items.title: A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation
items.abstract: Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. The factory processes configurable wafer lots with uniform and sinusoidal wafer arrival profiles and may undergo preventive maintenanc...

items.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $Γ$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. items.title: Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
items.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. These results constitute a step forward in practical i...

items.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
items.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the ex...

items.title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
items.abstract: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. items.title: DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration
items.abstract: Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. items.title: Porosification of the dielectric layer in alternating-current electroluminescence devices enables high-resolution tactile imaging
items.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. We identify a nonlinear capacitance-dependent emission window that provides a basis for tunable pressure-to-light conversion. Pore-size engineering further suppresses local emission deficiencies, reducing spatial intensity variation by nearly ninefold and enabling faithful imaging of contact features down to 100 μm. The continuous electroluminescent interface also reproduces complex contact patterns without computational rec...

items.title: Power Scaling Across Link Utilization with GPAM-4 Signaling and Event-Driven Reception
items.abstract: This work highlights the potential of combining event-based signaling with event-driven reception to achieve receiver power scaling across link utilization, without requiring wake-up, locking, or data-rate reconfiguration. The approach is demonstrated using the proposed four-level Gaussian pulse-amplitude modulation (GPAM-4) scheme and a corresponding event-driven receiver. By employing a resettable ring voltage-controlled oscillator (RRVCO) as its front end, the receiver achieves inherently event-driven symbol measurement, initiated directly by each received pulse. Symbols are decoded directly from the final RRVCO phase state, eliminating a counter-based back end. Simulated in 28-nm CMOS, the receiver power is evaluated across a $100\times$ range of effective data rates---from 0.15 mW at the peak rate of 8 Gb/s, down to 2.5 $μ$W under active/idle operation and 1.6 $μ$W under data rate c...

items.abstract: Next-generation implantable neurostimulators require efficient wireless power delivery in smaller, less invasive form factors, yet variations in tissue coupling, implantation conditions, and stimulation loads can alter received power (or requirements) and degrade energy-harvesting performance. This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. To validate the method, equation-based models are developed for seven circuit test cases in a commercial 65nm CMOS technology, covering 15 metrics on five operational transconductance amplifier topologies, and six metrics on two dynamic comparator topologies. When tested on 1000 unseen variants of these seven designs, each corresponding to a different set of independently sampled transistor sizes, the accuracy is found to be within 5% of SPICE. To demonstrate use cases for NEMESIS2.0, the generated models are used as performance evaluators in multiple transistor sizers based on different population-based stochastic search optimizers. items.title: On-demand valley control in a WSe2/CrPS4 heterostructure via optically programmed magnetic order
items.abstract: The ability to optically control the valley degree of freedom in two-dimensional semiconductors is critical for scalable valleytronics. While magnetic proximity effects can lift valley degeneracy, static interfaces lack the dynamic control needed for devices. Here, we demonstrate on-demand optical switching of valley symmetry breaking in a WSe2/CrPS4 heterostructure by exploiting light-tunable magnetic order. Using polarization- and time-resolved photoluminescence, we show that excitation below the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) gap preserves an out-of-plane Néel vector in CrPS4, generating a net out-of-plane spin at the interface and enabling spin-polarized charge transfer. This yields a robust polarization gap in the WSe2 A-exciton decay dynamics without an external magnetic field. items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnet...

items.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
items.abstract: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. Nominal results include 41.711 microwatts biased neuron-core power, 3.338-pJ positive terminal energy for a 1.4-microsecond cell read, and 0.531-mV selected-state drift over a 5-ms extracted-tile hold...

items.title: Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass
items.abstract: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors offer distinct advantages as imaging detectors for space-based X-ray observatories, being low-power, radiation-resistant, and operable at room temperature. Previous characterizations of the low-cost, commercially-available IMX290LLR-C back-illuminated CMOS sensor from Sony Semiconductor Solutions have found Fano-limited X-ray spectral resolutions while operated at room temperature and a radiation tolerance compatible with use in low Earth orbit. Here, we report the quantum efficiency of the IMX290LLR-C as measured across the soft X-ray band (200 - 1000 eV) using Beamline 6.3.2 of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. items.title: Characterization of the GIGAPYX-4600 CMOS visible image sensor in the context of high precision astrometry
items.abstract: To evaluate the potential of detectors for next-generation space astrometry missions such as the HWO and Theia, an extensive analysis of the performance of the GIGAPYX-4600 46-megapixel CMOS detector from Pyxalis was conducted at IPAG. The 5456x8320-pixel detector, featuring a 4.4-micron pitch and back-side illumination, constitutes a matrix of 24x36 mm. It has a measured gain of 13.3 electrons per ADU in low-gain mode. The saturation level of the detector in low-gain-mode is estimated to be approximately 52 000 electrons. This sensor demonstrates linearity errors of 0.90%, pixel response non-uniformity of less than 1.3%, and readout and quantization noise of 12 electrons in low-gain mode. Dark current was measured at 35 electrons per second at 35{\textdegree}C and inter-pixel capacitance remained under 3%. items.title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
items.abstract: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. items.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
items.abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. items.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
items.abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. items.title: CHARMING: Parallel Edge AI Acceleration Across Tensor Processing and In-Memory Computation
items.abstract: Edge AI increasingly relies on specialized accelerators for low-latency inference under tight resource and energy constraints, yet their efficiency remains limited by data movement. Prior work, CHARM, mitigates this overhead by overlapping data movement with computation. We observe that in-memory computing can further supplement tensor processing as a parallel accelerator while eliminating certain data movements entirely. We present CHARMING, a heterogeneous edge AI architecture that uses accuracy- and quantization-aware partitioning to distribute and concurrently execute inference workloads across tensor processing and in-memory computation. CHARMING partitions attention heads between an AIE array and an in-DRAM compute unit, balancing execution according to model architecture, sequence length, and precision while selecting heads to minimize accuracy degradation. items.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
items.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering...

items.title: SPLIT-MOR: Fast and Accurate Model Order Reduction for Nonlinear Transient Thermal Simulation of 2.5D/3D ICs
items.abstract: Fast and accurate transient thermal simulation is essential to thermal reliability analysis and dynamic thermal management of advanced packages, and model order reduction (MOR) techniques are widely applied to overcome the efficiency bottleneck of rigorous numerical methods. However, nonlinear terms including temperature-dependent leakage power, thermal conductivity, and heat capacity prevent the application of conventional linear MOR, while hyper-reduction solutions require costly nonlinear training data. In this work, we propose SPLIT-MOR (Subdomain-wise Piecewise Linearization with Interval Tensors), a novel nonlinear MOR method that requires no additional training set. SPLIT-MOR computes reduced component tensors by subdomain clustering and temperature-interval partitioning in the offline stage, and updates the reduced coefficient matrices and load vectors efficiently in the online s...

items.title: Contrastive local learning in large nonlinear analog circuits
items.abstract: Machine learning in physical hardware promises to reduce training cost by colocating computation, memory and adaptation within device physics. Contrastive local learning networks (CLLNs) offer a compelling route: an electrical circuit relaxes to equilibrium in free and weakly clamped states, and each adaptive element updates from local voltage contrasts rather than backpropagated error signals. Yet whether nonlinear transistor implementations can scale beyond proof-of-concept circuits, and what design principles control that scaling, have remained unknown. Here we show that nonlinear analog circuits trained by contrastive local rules can learn larger machine-learning tasks and remain robust under hardware nonidealities. Using device-level circuit simulations, we systematically explore initialization, operating regime, loss-dependent clamping and training parameters, and scale CLLNs beyon...

items.title: Composition Driven Band Alignment Evolution in Grafted Si/GeSn Heterostructures
items.abstract: Understanding and controlling band alignment in lattice-mismatched group-IV semiconductor-based heterostructures is fundamental to rational band-structure engineering, as it governs the electronic structure and carrier transport in heterointegrated semiconductor systems. Despite growing interest in Si/GeSn heterostructures, the composition-dependent band alignment has not been experimentally established. Here, we experimentally establish the evolution of band alignment in semiconductor-grafted Si/GeSn heterostructures with contents ranging from 8.8% to 12.4% using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Kraut's core-level method. The valence-band offset increases systematically from ~0.29 to ~0.57 eV with increasing Sn composition, whereas the corresponding effective conduction-band offset decreases from ~0.30 to ~0.12 eV. items.abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. items.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
items.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). items.title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs
items.abstract: New AI accelerators arrive before the kernels that make them fast, because peak kernel performance requires architecture-specific expertise in operand pipelines and data-movement techniques. Coding agents can now write, compile, and tune kernels on their own, so they could greatly accelerate kernel development and optimization. What agents produce depends on the interfaces they are given. These interfaces may expose a machine's raw capabilities or encode the known-good methods for exploiting its hardware features efficiently. We test the performance impact of these two interfaces on Intel GPUs through controlled experiments with five coding models on three kernels. With raw SYCL and execution feedback, Opus 4.8, the strongest of the three models tested with Claude Code, writes a single-GPU GEMM kernel reaching only 57.5% of Intel's tuned oneDNN library. items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive.
